question.text: Under FATF Special Recommendation IX (SR IX) on Cash Couriers, what mechanism must countries put in place to detect the physical cross-border transportation of currency and bearer negotiable instruments?

answer.text: A declaration system or other disclosure obligation
A prohibition system that bans all cross-border cash movement above a threshold
A permit system requiring prior government approval for any cash transportation
A mandatory reporting system where banks report all outward cash remittances

explanation.text: The Logic: SR IX requires countries to detect the physical cross-border transportation of currency and bearer negotiable instruments through a declaration system or other disclosure obligation. The standard targets physical cash courier movement, distinct from wire transfer monitoring. The Trap: A blanket prohibition or a permit-based prior-approval system goes beyond SR IX, which is a detection/transparency standard, not a ban. A bank-side reporting system addresses wire transfers, not physical cash courier movement. Note: SR IX is satisfied by either of two designs — a declaration system or a disclosure obligation — but it does not mandate any single threshold or operational design beyond the detection objective.
